title: WHERE: asking for only the rows you want

steps.title: The big new word: WHERE
steps.prompt:
SELECT picks the COLUMNS. WHERE picks the ROWS.
WHERE is a filter - imagine a sieve. Only the rows that pass through the holes stay.
WHERE price > 100 means: 'only rows whose price is above 100.'
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > 100;
hints: Start with SELECT name FROM products.
Add WHERE after FROM products.
Write the condition: price > 100.
Type: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > 100;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price > 100;

steps.title: Fill in the comparison symbol
steps.prompt:
SQL compares numbers with three little symbols:
 > means 'bigger than'    < means 'smaller than'    = means 'is exactly'
The query below should list products that are OUT OF STOCK (0 left).
One symbol is missing - it has been replaced by a blank ( ___ ).
Change the ___ so the query means 'stock is exactly 0':
SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock ___ 0;
steps.task: Replace the ___ with a symbol so it says 'stock is exactly 0'.
hints: A blank ( ___) sits where a symbol should be. Delete it and type a symbol.
We want 'stock is exactly 0' - not bigger than 0 and not smaller than 0.
The symbol for 'is exactly' is one equals sign.
Final query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock = 0;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock = 0;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock ___ 0;

steps.title: Text needs little wings
steps.prompt:
Words in SQL are written inside single quotes, like little wings: 'Marrakech'.
Numbers never need quotes - only text does.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Marrakech';
hints: Start with SELECT name, city FROM customers.
Add WHERE city = …
Wrap Marrakech in single quotes.
Type: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Marrakech';
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Marrakech';

steps.title: Fix the double equals
steps.task: Fix the query so it returns products with zero stock.
hints: Something is doubled.
In SQL, one equals sign means 'is exactly'.
One = is enough. Two is a mistake here.
Change == to a single =.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock = 0;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock == 0;
steps.memory_trick: Exactly one equals sign in SQL.

steps.title: Predict: how many?
steps.task: How many products cost more than 100 MAD?
hints: This query filters with price > 100.
count(*) counts the rows that pass.
Run it to check your guess - prediction lets you peek.
Answer: 21.
steps.memory_trick: Predicting numbers trains your database intuition.
